chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Joining Ray Noble at the Rainbow Room
summary: Pee Wee Erwin, Mondello and Freeman join Ray Noble's American band at the Rainbow Room, with Glenn Miller, Claude Thornhill, Bill Harty and Spivak.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Then, from that job Toots Mondello and I got an offer and Pee Wee Erwin, the three of us got an offer to go with Ray Noble. Now, as you know, Ray Noble was a fine musician who had made a lot of recordings here in England and was not allowed to bring the whole band in to the States because of some labor law condition that existed or may still exist and so he brought Al Bawly, who was a very good singer in those days -- we are not talking about jazz now, we are talking about dance bands.

MR. FREEMAN: And he brought his drummer-manager, Bill Harty, who was a damn good musician and we played in a place called the Rainbow Room. Now, in those days, it was white tie and tails, tiara and slippers, very posh and we worked in tuxedos, and we had in that band Claude Thornhill on piano, who was later to become a famous bandleader. I cannot remember the name of the bass player. Bill Harty played drums. We had Wilbur Schwichtenberg, who later became Will Bradley, the bandleader, a fine

trombone player. Glenn Miller, Pee Wee Erwin, Charlie Mince, Spivak, Toots Mondello, myself, Johnny Mince, who is very much on the scene today, fine clarinet player and George -- oh, dear, the great guitarist, George Van Epps, a super musician.
I cannot remember the other players in the band, but we had a ball and --
Now, if you are going to change this over, do it now, because I got a wonderful story to tell you about Ray Noble.
Really, when you called the lineup on that band, there'd be few bands of anybody's band that you could call a lineup like that. I don't think the Goodman band would be any finer, would it?

Well, of course, Benny was in another type of music and we were -- but it was dance music, of course. Our band was not -- Noble's band was not a jazz band in any sense, excepting that he allowed me to play and he allowed Pee Wee to play and so --
